product.title: ESPN Crisis Manager: The Salary Cap Leak
product.summary: Eight rounds of crisis management after undisclosed payments leak.
product.whatStudentsDo: Students act as an executive VP after a leak reveals payments made outside the stated cap. Each of eight rounds moves trust, legal exposure, revenue and control, and the story branches between defending transparency and defending legally, through fines, lost picks and sponsor reactions.

studentDataProfile.notes: State kept in browser localStorage only; no server call observed.

governance.maturityBasis: Complete and publicly reachable with full path branching. No student-run evidence exists.

health.technicalBasis: Playtested end to end 2026-08-16. The strongest narrative writing in the account and the most dramatic divergence measured anywhere: a combative run collapsed to trust 0 and revenue 0 for 26/100, a cooperative run held trust 100 for 95/100, and the branch genuinely locks in by round 8. Undermined by an ordering exploit.
knownBlockers: Clicking the first option every round without reading scored 95 out of 100 and the top "Crisis Captain" tier. Shuffling option order per round would remove it.
Visually the plainest of the 301-tier simulations — a flat background and unstyled meters next to the dashboard treatment its siblings use.

curation.tierBasis: The most dramatic consequence divergence measured — trust 0 and revenue 0 against a 95 out of 100 run — and excellent writing. Clicking the first option every round scores 95 without reading, which shuffling option order would fix.
